notes: Kit consists of one transmitter (TX) and one receiver (RX); ports are prefixed accordingly. Both units also have a rear Sony NP-F battery lock/mount for battery power, but this is a mechanical battery slide-mount rather than a cable connector, so it is not represented as a port. Neither HDMI nor USB-C speed/version grades are stated anywhere in manufacturer materials (only resolution/frame-rate: 1080p up to 60fps) or the user manual, so grade is omitted on all ports per instructions. DC input spec (5.5x2.1mm barrel, 7.4-16.8V) and the single dual-purpose USB-C port on the receiver (UVC out + power in) were cross-confirmed against the official CineView HE user manual (manuals.plus mirror of manualslib.com/manual/2592347) in addition to the manufacturer product page. Desktop/handheld unit, not rack-mountable, so rackUnits omitted. Category mapped to "converter" and type to "Extender" as the closest fit for a wireless HDMI transmission (TX/RX) system - no dedicated "wireless video transmitter" category/type exists in the given enums.

ports.name: TX HDMI In
ports.note: Transmitter video input from camera, up to 1080p60. HDMI version not stated by manufacturer.

ports.name: TX HDMI Out (Loop)
ports.note: Zero-latency lossless HDMI loop-out on transmitter for a local monitor.

ports.name: TX USB-C
ports.note: 5V/2A power input only on transmitter; no data/UVC function.

ports.name: RX HDMI Out
ports.note: Receiver video output to monitor, up to 1080p60. HDMI version not stated by manufacturer.

ports.name: RX USB-C (UVC Out)
ports.note: Single physical USB-C port that both streams UVC video out to a computer/phone (webcam-style live streaming) and accepts 5V/2A power input.
